title: A Letter from Jonas
notebook: Jonas read my letter three times: anger, then sadness, then understanding.
He says I am afraid of losing them. He will wait for me to come back as Katerin.

narrative.text: Jonas places a small, folded note on the kitchen table next to your coffee. It is in his handwriting — the careful, architectural script of a man who draws buildings for a living. It is a reply to your letter. He has written it on the back of an old blueprint.

I read your letter three times. The first time I was angry — I thought it was too little, too late, another way of being present without being here. The second time I was sad. The third time I understood what you were actually saying. You are afraid you are losing us. You are. But we are still here. I am still here. When you are ready to come back — not the Chancellor, just Katerin — I will be waiting.

monologue: Three readings. Anger, then sadness, then understanding. He gave me the arc I did not give him. When he says 'just Katerin,' he means the person who existed before the office consumed her. Find her. She is still in here somewhere.

choices.text: "...Thank you, Jonas. For waiting. For understanding. For all of it."

reactions.text: He does not speak. He simply reaches across the table and puts his hand over yours — the gesture that has meant I am still here for twenty years. The blueprint underneath his note is still there. So is he.
